summary: Hojun Nagasaki specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, served as a professor emeritus at Otani University (~1969–1999), and was president of the Japan Association of Jain Studies in 1998.
Hokei Izumi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University, where he also served as a professor (attested 1930).
Hoko Kuwana works in the field of Buddhist studies. Kuwana studied at Rissho University (attested 2015) and held a post as department director at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She was a doctoral candidate in Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at Harvard University (~2001–2009) and took up a post at the University of Colorado Boulder around 2009.

Holmes Welch worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. After earning a B.A. and M.A. at Harvard University (~1940–1957), he taught as a lecturer at Harvard and Yale, and served as deputy director of the Center for the Study of World Religions.

Hong Luo works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Luo completed doctoral studies at Peking University and held posts at the China Tibetology Research Center, Sichuan University as professor, and the University of Hamburg as a research fellow (attested 2026).

Hongyue Guo specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Guo completed a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2007) under doctoral supervisor Stephen R. Bokenkamp, and also studied under teacher Xubang Qi.

Honsho Ueda is a Buddhist studies scholar. Ueda served as lecturer (attested 1963) and professor (attested 1992) at Minobusan Junior College, and as professor at Minobusan University and director of the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (both attested 1996).
Hoong Teik Toh works in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Harvard University in 2004, having studied under teachers Gray Tuttle, Ruohong Li, and Yudru Tsomu.

Horace Hayman Wilson was an Indologist who studied medicine at St Thomas' Hospital Medical School (~1804–1808). He served as Boden Professor of Sanscrit at the University of Oxford (1831–1860) and librarian for the East India Company and India Office Library.

Horace L. Friess specialized in religious studies and philosophy. He earned his bachelor's at Columbia University (~1915–1918) and studied at Heidelberg University, later serving at Johns Hopkins and Columbia, where he was Buttenwieser Professor of Human Relations (1962–1966).
Horst Brinkhaus is a scholar in the field of Indology. He held posts at the University of Münster (attested 1978) and at Kiel University (~1993–2008).

Horst Lasic specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed a PhD at the University of Vienna in 1999, served as a research fellow at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (1995), and lectured at the University of Vienna (1999).

Hosakote Krishna Sastri was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He served as an epigraphist for the Archaeological Survey of India (~1891–1925) and as Government Epigraphist for India (~1920–1925).

Hoseok Leigh specializes in philosophy and religious studies. Leigh earned a PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2010), having studied under teacher Ha-u Kim and traditional teacher Cheonghwa.
Hoseong Kim is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Kim served as a professor at Dongguk University and founded the Nihon Bukkyoshi Kenkyujo (both attested 2011).
Hoshu Mitsuhara is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Mitsuhara held posts at Koyasan University as professor (attested 1982) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2004).

Hotetsu Matsumoto specializes in Buddhist studies. Matsumoto held an affiliation at Tohoku University (attested 1997) and served as professor and director of the Clinical Esoteric Buddhism Center at Shuchiin University (attested 2026).

Houn Jiyu-Kennett was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Durham University, Trinity Laban, and Soji-ji (1962–1963). She served as head priest at Unpuku-ji and as abbess of Shasta Abbey until 1996, which she founded in 1970.

Howard Zinn was a historian who studied at New York University (~1949–1951) and Columbia University (~1951–1958). He held posts at Spelman College (1956–1963), Harvard University (1960–1961), and Boston University (1964–1988), where he became professor emeritus.
